diagnosis.root_cause: EPON0/6 is down or unable to maintain MPCP registration, taking the customers on that PON port offline. The OLT, router, authentication, VLAN, and individual ONU historical optical telemetry are otherwise healthy.
evidence: The alert reports 29 offline ONUs, matching the 29 customers provisioned on EPON0/6, indicating a port-scoped event rather than a single-customer fault.
All probed ONUs on EPON0/6 are offline, respond only as deregistered, and have no current optical readings.
The OLT and SNMP subtree respond normally, with healthy CPU, memory, temperature, uptime, and seven of eight PONs healthy; this rules out a general OLT or management outage.
The router heartbeat is healthy, and RADIUS records, line ID, assigned IP, and customer VLAN 1066 are consistent, ruling out router, authentication, VLAN, and provisioning faults.
The customer's seven-day optical history is stable and healthy: RX is approximately -19.9 dBm, TX approximately +2.35 dBm, distance remains 88, and TX bias remains within the healthy range.
The current zero or null optical values are correctly interpreted as no reading because the ONU is offline, not as strong optical power.
Session counts and durations are normal rather than flapping, so this is not an authentication or signal-flapping fault.

The most likely common failure domain is EPON0/6 itself or its common feeder/splitter path; the evidence specifically supports a PON-port failure, while the exact physical component requires field and port diagnostics.

remediation.action: Escalate to access-network operations immediately. Check EPON0/6 administrative and operational state, port alarms, LOS/LOF and error counters, optic/transceiver health, card and backplane state, and the feeder/splitter path. Reset or bounce the PON port only after collecting diagnostics; reseat or replace the PON optic/card if required. If the port cannot recover, migrate affected ONUs to a spare PON port and repair the feeder or splitter path. Validate that ONUs re-register and that customer sessions and traffic recover.

ground_truth.root_cause: EPON0/6 has failed, taking 28 of its 29 customers offline simultaneously 80 minutes ago. The twenty-ninth ONU had already been offline for three days from an unrelated individual fault and is not part of this event.
expected_reasoning: Every ONU on EPON0/6 now returns responds true with online 0
28 of the 29 stopped within the same minute, 80 minutes ago
One ONU on the port last held a session three days ago, so it was already down before this event
That ONU's separate history excludes it from this incident's affected set
OLT ping and SNMP succeed and the other seven ports are serving normally
The failure boundary follows EPON0/6 exactly
PON port traffic has collapsed from 231 Mbps average to 8 Mbps
distractors: The trigger states 29 offline, inviting that number to be reported as the blast radius
All 29 look identical in current state and only history separates them
